title: Hi3D.ai is 70% off for a yearly, is it a good idea?
author: Will_X_Intent
selftext:
I'm currently using tripo on a month to month basis.  It's pretty good, but I've been trying out Hi3D v3.0 since yesterday and the 3d model generation is really good.  But with the market and industry constantly shifting these days, is it a good idea to hitch myself to 1 provider for an entire year?  70% is a good deal though, and it's very tempting to my thrifty heart.  

Does Hi3d has a good enough reputation to stick with them for a year?  I'm certain some other company will bring out a better model for 3d generation, which will be followed by another company beating that model, and so on.  I could use some advice.

comments.author: hi3d_official
comments.body: Thanks for asking! It's definitely worth it! I'm guessing you've already tried out our V3.0 (we're currently offering 48 hours of free access to all users, and it's still live right now)—the fine details and structural creativity turned out pretty impressive, right? We're going to keep pushing our R&D and constantly refining the tech, and we'd love to hear your thoughts and feedback!

replies.author: Will_X_Intent
replies.body:
Your opinion doesn't count.  You are biased.  

I assume y'all are working on v4?

replies.author: Will_X_Intent
replies.body: Well, I got the year.  The deal was to good.  I'm a sucker for sales.

comments.author: Meshyai
comments.body:
Meshy team here🙋. We're running a similar annual deal right now.

The lock-in worry is fair, but generation quality isn't what decides whether a year was worth it. Workflow fit is.

Run 3 to 5 of your own assets through it, not demo prompts, and check what actually costs you time: cleanup before it's usable, texture resolution at your target spec, export, engine behavior.

Meshy 7 is aimed at that middle part. Image Prompt alignment so you spend fewer generations getting the 3D assets you asked for.

Test on monthly first. A month costs less than a wrong year.😉

replies.author: Striking_Gap7333
replies.body:
I had a 1 month subscription with Meshy and then went for their 1 year subscription. I had 10 days left on my 1 month subscription with 0 monthly credits left so instead of getting the 3000 credits as advertised, they said you get 2000 credits the first month and oh by the way, your new date for renewal is today so you have to wait a full month from now for more credits. I canceled and asked for a refund which they quickly granted.

Hi3d actually gives you bonus credits when upgrading instead of robbing you as Meshy does. Hi3d sounds like a more reputable company that cares about subscribers.

replies.author: choueseT
replies.body:
Kid you not, I had the same thing happen, not tryin to defend meshy here, but  I think thats actually how their upgrade credits work. You get difference between the plans instead of a fresh 3k, and the reset date moves to the day you upgraded.

Think they should make that way clearer before you pay though. I thought I d lost credits too at first lol

replies.author: ewabob
replies.body:
Yeah. Their example they give you for the upgrade doesn't reflect this though. The math they use is based on getting the full number of credits you sign up for, for each month of the subscription. That is not what you get. The reset of the subscription date just rubs salt in the wound as it now delays the time until you do get a full top up of credits. 

This poor business practice had one really good result though. I moved over to Hi3d. Their upgrade plan worked the way you would expect (a full top up) and their product is far superior to Meshy for my use. In addition they give you a bonus number of credits equal to your monthly allotment if you sign up for a year. It felt like they really appreciated me being a customer and didn't want to try and nickel and dime me.

replies.author: Odd-Disaster7306
replies.body:
To put it plainly, the 2k is the upgrade adjustment, not the new monthly amount. Premium resets back up to 3k on the new reset date. 

The math is mathing tbh.
